subject: VPC maintenance: proposed MOP, window stagger & rollback criteria
messages:
From: laura_bennett@redwood.com
To: Rajesh Patel <rajesh@acme-fin.com>
Cc: vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com, aditya_rao@redwood.com
Date: Sat, 01 Aug 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: VPC maintenance: proposed MOP, window stagger & rollback criteria

Hi Rajesh,

Thanks again for the sync earlier — attached is Redwood's proposed Method of Procedure (MOP) for the private VPC maintenance we discussed (acme_mop_v2.pdf). High level: a minor runtime/security patch (runtime 1.2.3 -> 1.2.4) to address a CVE in a third-party kernel, and a small config tweak to KV cache TTLs.

We want to propose a staggered maintenance approach so we can preserve the SLA for critical routes while finishing the patch across your noncritical pools. Key asks from your side:
- Confirm a 4-hour maintenance window where traffic can be shifted (we recommend 02:00-06:00 UTC on Aug 3).
- Identify the pair of control-plane bastion IPs that we should use for out-of-band access during the window.
- Approve canary scope: 5% of prod traffic routed to a dedicated canary pool for 20 minutes.

Summary of our rollback criteria (full checklist in rollback_checklist.xlsx):
1) Error rate > 1.5x baseline for 10 consecutive minutes
2) Median tail latency increase > 200ms (p95) for 5 minutes
3) Any KV cache corruption detected by checksums during warming
4) Failed health-check drains or inability to rejoin nodes after reboot

Operational steps in the MOP include: draining one worker rack at a time, applying the runtime patch, restarting the serving runtime with pinned model variant set to v1.2 (we will not change model weights), warming KV caches, and running synthetic prompts against the canary. If canary passes, we ramp to the next 10% (5 -> 15 -> 50 -> 100) with 15-minute stability gates.

I've cc'd Vivek and Aditya to handle infra access and the rollout orchestration. Vivek — can you confirm the rollout playbook and whether we should use the automated rollout or run each ramp manually? Aditya — please double-check the configuration changes in the patch and the expected warmup time for the largest shard.

We will also attach a short DocuSign change-order for your records if you want Redwood to act as the operator for the window.

Regards,

Laura Bennett
Head of Sales, Enterprise
Redwood Inference

+1 (415) 555-0123

On Sat, Aug 1, 2026 at 09:12 AM Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com> wrote:
> Hi Rajesh,
> 
> Thanks again for the sync earlier — attached is Redwood's proposed Method of Procedure (MOP) for the private VPC maintenance we discussed (acme_mop_v2.pdf).

Thanks Laura — this looks thorough. A few quick confirmations from our side:
- Window: Aug 3, 02:00-06:00 UTC works for our ops rotation team.
- Bastion IPs: ops@acme-fin.com will send a signed one-time SSH key via your SRE channel; we will not expose the permanent jump IP.
- Canary: 5% for 20 minutes OK. We want an explicit fail-open option if the canary experiences transient errors (so we do not immediately take out all traffic).

Two asks/questions:
1) Can you add a step to validate audit logs and request tracing immediately after the KV cache warm? We want to ensure no trace gaps for our compliance audit.
2) If rollback is triggered, how long until we can return to baseline (approx)? Our procurement team needs an estimate for downtime windows when we file this to change control.

I'll wait for Vivek and Aditya to confirm the finer points.

- Rajesh
Rajesh Patel
Head of Platform Ops
Acme Financial
rajesh@acme-fin.com
From: vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com

Date: Sun, 02 Aug 2026 07:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: VPC maintenance: proposed MOP, window stagger & rollback criteria

On Sat, Aug 1, 2026 at 01:47 PM Rajesh Patel <rajesh@acme-fin.com> wrote:
> Thanks Laura — this looks thorough. A few quick confirmations from our side:
> - Window: Aug 3, 02:00-06:00 UTC works for our ops rotation team.
> - Bastion IPs: ops@acme-fin.com will send a signed one-time SSH key via your SRE channel; we will not expose the permanent jump IP.

Thanks — quick responses below:
- Rollout automation: recommend automated ramp via our Rollout Engine with manual approval gates at 20% and 50%. I will be on-call for the window and can approve fast if metrics look clean.
- Audit logs & tracing: agreed — we'll run the post-warm validation script (validate_audit_and_traces.sh) immediately after KV cache warm and before promoting canary. I'll add it to step 6 of the MOP.
- Rollback duration: if rollback triggered during a single rack patch, baseline return time is ~8-12 minutes after we switch traffic back and rehydrate caches; for a full-pool rollback expect 30-45 minutes to stabilize (network drains + cache warms). Put another way: worst case 45 minutes to baseline.

Two operational notes for Acme:
1) We'll pin the serving runtime binary and the model-variant tag for the window (no model weight changes). Pinning avoids incidental changes during restart.
2) We will enable the circuit-breaker flag on critical routes so that failures route to a protected fallback rather than cascading. This will cause transient increase in 503s but prevents full outage.

Aditya, can you confirm the warmup numbers for the largest shard (expected 12 minutes to reach steady p95 for token latency) and whether the warm script is idempotent if run twice?

-Vivek
Vivek Kulkarni
Senior SRE, Redwood Inference

On Sun, Aug 2, 2026 at 07:05 AM Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com> wrote:
> Thanks — quick responses below:
> - Rollout automation: recommend automated ramp via our Rollout Engine with manual approval gates at 20% and 50%.
> - Audit logs & tracing: agreed — we'll run the post-warm validation script (validate_audit_and_traces.sh) immediately after KV cache warm and before promoting canary.
> - Rollback duration: ... worst case 45 minutes to baseline.

Confirmed on my side: warmup numbers are conservative; largest shard steady-state p95 usually reached in 9-14 minutes depending on traffic mix — we will assume 12 minutes as the planning number. The warm script is idempotent and includes checksums for KV cache to catch any corruption; it logs to the /var/log/redwood/warmup.log and emits an event to your audit endpoint when done.

I added one extra safety gate to the MOP: after the first successful rack patch and canary pass, we will run a smoke-run of three representative prompts (short completion, structured function call, and embedding request) against the canary and verify semantic fidelity against a small baseline prompt set. That lowers the risk of a hidden inference regression.

If everyone is aligned I'll mark the MOP final and push a signed DocuSign change-order for your records.

-Aditya Rao
Principal Platform Engineer
Redwood Inference
